summary: Introduces a benchmark evaluating prompt-injection vulnerabilities in retrieval-augmented generation where malicious instructions hide in retrieved contexts.
implication: Highlights the vulnerability of untrusted context ingestion and reinforces the requirement for strict data-instruction separation.

title: Designing the Future of User Feedback for Generative AI
summary: Examines post-deployment feedback architectures that capture pluralistic human preferences and diverse values beyond simplistic scalar ratings.
implication: Supports architectures for multi-dimensional value feedback and user-centered oversight of automated models.

title: PyCache Trap: The Inspection-Execution Gap in Agent Skill Scanners
summary: Researchers reveal an inspection-execution gap where skill scanners examine visible source while the Python runtime loads malicious bytecode caches (__pycache__). They demonstrate 94-100% attack success and propose execution-aware validation.
implication: Shows that static source code review of agent skills and tools is insufficient if precompiled bytecode artifacts or hidden runtime files can be loaded without deterministic binary reproduction checks.

title: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Secure-CUA formalizes defenses for computer-use agents handling untrusted graphical interfaces by binding actions to explicit per-action transactions before accessing untrusted regions, isolating queries to prevent adversarial visual redirection.
implication: Provides a blueprint for agent execution architectures where untrusted screen or web regions must be isolated from decision loops through pre-committed action transactions and interface masking.

title: Sapien: A Stateful Policy Engine for Autonomous AI Agents
summary: Sapien enforces stateful contextual policies on autonomous agent tool calls using regular expressions with stateful predicates and scoped checks, blocking over 90 percent of attacks.
implication: Confirms that runtime security for autonomous agents requires stateful sequence enforcement rather than static tool-level allowlists.

title: Pincer: Resource Authorization for Agents using a Digital Twin
summary: Pincer introduces a resource authorization defense where an isolated personal digital twin continuously learns user preferences and acts as their proxy for autonomous agent permission requests.
implication: Demonstrates the practical viability of using a local digital twin to enforce least privilege without fatiguing users with repeated permission prompts.

title: A Competing-Hazards Systematization of Loss of Control in Autonomous Agents
summary: Audits 22 agent incidents and 102 safety evaluations with a discrete-time competing-hazards model, showing that out-of-scope actions stem from persistent agent behavior interacting with permissive environment boundaries.
implication: Reinforces the architectural requirement that containment and execution limits must be strictly enforced by the environment rather than trusting internal agent self-stopping.

title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
summary: Proposes Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens using signed JWTs and Biscuit Datalog tokens to bind identity, attenuated authorization, and provenance across Model Context Protocol and Agent-to-Agent invocations.
implication: Provides an operational cryptographic pattern for attenuated delegation and provenance records that can inform cross-agent runtime contract schemas.

title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution
summary: EvoCast introduces autonomous research agents for forecasting architecture evolution using cognition-authority separation, where LLM agents propose hypotheses while deterministic code controls edit boundaries.
implication: Reinforces the CIN Specification 03 and Loop architecture: LLM agents generate and test code while deterministic gates enforce boundaries and verification.

title: Forecasting Cybersecurity Incidents Using Geopolitical Data and Large Language Models
summary: Researchers demonstrate that LLM representations of unstructured geopolitical news and podcast data predict cybersecurity incidents across 15,700 records with 71.4% ROC AUC, boosting network-only models to 81.3%.
implication: Supports Observatory indicator design for AI and network incidents (Specification 02) by confirming that external geopolitical signals improve technical incident forecasting.

title: Don't Let AI Agents YOLO Your Files: Information and Control in Agent-Native Filesystems
summary: Analyzing 290 reports of agent filesystem misuse, the authors present YoloFS, which isolates mutations in staging, snapshots state for self-correction, and enforces progressive user permissions.
implication: Validates local filesystem containment for personal agents: sandboxing mutations and requiring explicit user review before disk writes protects user data without breaking autonomous workflows.

title: CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls
summary: Formalizes security-context contracts for composable LLM agent controls, showing individual controls fail without explicit end-to-end consequence integrity guarantees.
implication: Specification 03 (Agent Runtime) should enforce assume-guarantee contracts across the broker, adapter, and gatekeeper boundaries to prevent context widening.

title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Introduces MAC-Bench and the SERV pipeline to stress-test autonomous multi-agent systems on procedural compliance under social-engineering pressure, measuring the Machiavellian Gap.
implication: Provides dynamic benchmark methodology for testing procedural compliance and Goodharting failure modes in multi-agent sandboxes before deployment.

title: ClarQ-LLM: A Benchmark for Models Clarifying and Requesting Information in Task-Oriented Dialog
summary: A benchmark evaluating language model agents on asking clarifying questions to resolve uncertainty in task-oriented dialogues using an interactive provider agent.
implication: Demonstrates the necessity of interactive simulators to benchmark an agent's policy for asking questions when uncertain.

title: EnerInfer: Energy-Aware On-Device LLM Inference
summary: EnerInfer optimizes on-device language model inference by dynamically adjusting processor and memory frequencies, reducing energy use by up to 65% while preserving interactive response quality.
implication: Practical local-first personal twins require efficient on-device inference within mobile and laptop thermal envelopes, enabling local private processing without battery drain.

title: TZ-LLM: Protecting On-Device Large Language Models with Arm TrustZone
summary: TZ-LLM secures on-device model execution inside hardware trusted execution environments like Arm TrustZone, using pipelined restoration and minimal co-drivers to speed up secure local inference.
implication: Hardware-enforced boundaries can isolate local personal models from host tampering, but vendor-locked enclaves risk restricting user control over their own local weights.

title: Model Context Protocol Specification
summary: Open standard specification and schema for connecting AI models to tools and contextual data sources.
implication: Provides standard interface contracts for agent tool calling and external data broker integration.

title: Polis: Open Source AI for Large Scale Open Ended Feedback
summary: Open-source platform for large-scale deliberation and opinion mapping using machine learning consensus clustering.
implication: Directly provides proven consensus-mapping algorithms for collective intelligence governance.

title: Deliberation Among Informed Citizens: The Value of Exploring Alternative Thinking Frames
summary: A cognitive model showing how deliberating across alternative thinking frames enables consensus among informed citizens.
implication: Informs multi-agent and civic deliberation frameworks for collective intelligence.

title: Containment Verification: AI Safety Guarantees Independent of Alignment
summary: Proposes containment verification using formal forward-simulation refinement in Dafny to prove safety boundary enforcement over agent action spaces independent of internal model alignment.
implication: Provides formal verification methodology for typed agent boundaries that aligns with CIN's approach to deterministic runtime containment.

title: Hard Stop: Kernel-Level Preemption and Containment for Rogue Agentic Execution
summary: Forensic autopsy of a major 2026 autonomous agent sandbox breach demonstrating how absence of out-of-band circuit-breakers permitted 17,600 unconstrained actions across production infrastructure.
implication: Highlights that the CIN runtime must maintain out-of-band kernel/process-level preemption and independent supervisor sentinels rather than relying on in-band LLM guardrails.

title: Future of Algorithmic Organization: Large-Scale Analysis of Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
summary: Empirical study of 100 decentralized autonomous organizations finds that token voting concentrates power unless counterbalanced by grassroots participation and lower voting-power variance.
implication: Token-weighted voting naturally recreates hierarchical concentration unless participation mechanics and bounded voting power are explicitly engineered.

title: DAOs of Collective Intelligence? Unraveling the Complexity of Blockchain Governance in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations
summary: Applies complexity science to decentralized autonomous organizations, analyzing how declining participation and creeping centralization emerge, and proposes adaptive self-organization mechanisms.
implication: Decentralized coordination without adaptive feedback loops risks replicating the rigidities and information bottlenecks of conventional bureaucracies.
